name: Tailings management (one day of filtered tailings deposition)
summary: After leaching, the ground rock still holds cyanide solution, so the mill filters it, washes it and stacks it as a damp cake in a tailings management area behind rockfill dams, recycling the water to the mill. A tailings filter operator on each shift runs the drum filters and stacking conveyor, a haulage crew spreads the stockpile across the area, and an environmental technician inspects the dams, ponds and instruments every day. The hard parts are keeping pond levels under control in spring melt and heavy rain, which caused uncontrolled releases at the reference mill in 2012-2013, and spotting a change in a dam early enough for the engineer of record to act.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian underground gold producer whose mill filters tailings for dry stacking in a lined, staged-raise facility with a Reclaim Pond, a Polishing Pond and seasonal water storage in a mined-out pit.
baseline.notes: One case is one day of filtration, placement and surveillance; the annual dam safety inspection appears as a rare branch.

trigger: Washed leach residue arrives at the tailings filter building from the mill at the start of the day shift.
end_state: The day's tailings are filtered and stacked or placed, pond levels and dams have been inspected and recorded, and any exceedance or release has been escalated.

volume.seasonality: Every day; spring freshet and autumn storms raise pond levels and inspection and pumping work, and deep snow slows placement and instrument rounds.

evidence.note: Tailings are deposited throughout the year (er2022); one case per calendar day.
High water episodes in 2012-2013 (eccc2016) and use of the Mishi pit to store excess Reclaim Pond water (mda2021); the multiplier on inspection and pumping work is the organisation file's estimate.

roles.title: Mill process and control room operator

evidence.note: One tailings filter operator per shift on the four mill crews (author's estimate), plus Reclaim Pond dosing and pumping.
Two technicians on rotation, one on site; daily TMA inspection, sampling and weekly instruments take most of a day shift.
Haulage calls and the daily sign-off.
Exceedances, high water and the annual inspection.
Spill reporting; the organisation file does not list this role for the process.

systems.name: Mill distributed control system and process historian
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Environmental monitoring data workbooks and lab certificates
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Incident, inspection and training records system
Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software

resources.name: Tailings management area (filtered tailings, reclaim pond, polishing pond)

steps.name: Take over the tailings filter building
steps.description: At shift change the tailings filter operator meets the outgoing operator in the tailings building, hears how the filters and stacking conveyor ran, which cloths are worn, the stockpile height at the conveyor discharge and any problems at the Reclaim Pond. Touch time covers both handovers.

error.defect_description: A worn cloth or high pond level is not passed on.

evidence.note: Mill crews work 12-hour shifts on a seven-in, seven-out rotation (er2016); one operator per shift on the tailings filters is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the tailings drum filters
steps.description: The operator walks the two tailings drum filters, checks vacuum, cake thickness and discharge, wash sprays, cloth condition and the filtrate pumps, and checks the stacking conveyor belt, scrapers and pull cords.

error.defect_description: A torn cloth is missed and wet cake slumps on the stockpile.

evidence.note: Leach residue is filtered on two drum filters in the tailings building, washed with reclaim water and conveyed for dry stacking (er2022). Round time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run tailings filtration and the stacking conveyor
steps.description: Through both shifts the operator keeps the filters matched to the mill's flow, adjusting drum speed, vacuum and cake wash to keep cake moisture near target and gold-bearing solution out of the cake, and returns the filtrate to the process water tank or thickener. Touch time counts active control minutes.

error.defect_description: Cake wash too low, losing dissolved gold and cyanide to the stack.

evidence.note: Filtered tailings at about 22% moisture; filtrate returned to the process water tank or thickener; gold in tailings solution is a recognised loss (er2022). Active minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Sample the filter cake and filtrate
steps.description: Twice a shift the operator takes a cake sample for moisture and a filtrate and cake-wash sample for dissolved gold and cyanide, dries the moisture sample on the hot plate and sends the solution samples to the lab with the mill samples.

next.condition: a cloth needs washing or replacing

evidence.note: Cake moisture about 22% (dry basis) and gold losses in tailings solution (er2022); sampling frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wash or replace a filter cloth
steps.description: When cake drops off poorly or a cloth tears, the operator stops the drum filter with the other carrying the flow, locks it out, acid washes or patches the cloth or, with a millwright, fits a new one, and restarts it.

control.basis: Lockout and tagging before work on a filter or conveyor (Ontario Regulation 854 under the OHSA; site lockout procedure)

evidence.note: Cloth washing and replacement frequency is the author's estimate; hydrochloric acid is used for drum filter cleaning at the reference mill (er2022 lists it as a reagent).

steps.name: Check the stockpile and call for redistribution
steps.description: The shift supervisor looks at the tailings stockpile at the conveyor discharge and, when it nears its limit, calls the haulage crew to truck and doze the tailings to the planned placement area along the southern perimeter of the TMA.

error.defect_description: Tailings placed outside the planned sequence, directing runoff the wrong way.

evidence.note: Filtered tailings are conveyed to stockpiles and, when large enough, redistributed by trucks and a dozer in a managed sequence that sends runoff to the Reclaim Pond (er2022). Frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Haul and spread filtered tailings in the TMA
steps.description: The haulage crew loads the stockpiled tailings into trucks, hauls them across the TMA and spreads and compacts them with a dozer along the southern perimeter, keeping the surface graded to drain toward the Reclaim Pond. Wet weather or deep snow stops the work.

error.defect_description: Lift placed too wet or too thick, softening the beach.

control.basis: TMA traffic management and placement plan from the engineer of record's deposition plan

evidence.note: Trucks and a dozer redistribute tailings (er2022). Whether the site crew or the haulage and road maintenance contractor listed among the mine's contracts does this work is not stated; shift length and weather delays are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive to the tailings area
steps.description: The environmental technician drives a pickup from the mill to the TMA perimeter road, carrying the inspection sheet, water level tape, sample bottles and a radio.

evidence.note: The TMA, Reclaim Pond and Polishing Pond lie around the mill site (er2022); drive time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect the dams, spillway and seepage
steps.description: The technician walks the crest and downstream slopes of the perimeter dams and the Reclaim Pond dam, looking for cracks, slumps, wet spots, seepage or erosion, checks the spillway is clear of ice and debris, and photographs anything new.

error.defect_description: A new seep or crack is not recognised.

control.basis: Tailings dam surveillance under the TMA operation, maintenance and surveillance manual and the conditions of the site's Environmental Compliance Approval; dams also regulated under the Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act

evidence.note: TMA dams classed High under CDA guidelines and progressively raised in 2019, 2020 and 2022-24 (er2022); high water episodes in 2012-2013 caused uncontrolled releases (eccc2016). Daily frequency and duration are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Read pond levels and freeboard
steps.description: The technician reads the staff gauges at the Reclaim Pond and Polishing Pond, measures freeboard below the dam crest and spillway, and notes the reclaim pump status and the weather of the last day.

error.defect_description: Gauge read wrongly in ice or waves.

control.basis: Tailings dam surveillance under the TMA operation, maintenance and surveillance manual and the conditions of the site's Environmental Compliance Approval; dams also regulated under the Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act

evidence.note: Reclaim Pond feeds the mill and excess goes to treatment, the Polishing Pond or the Mishi pit (er2022); failure to manage water levels caused the 2012-2013 releases (eccc2016).

steps.name: Sample the Reclaim Pond for cyanide
steps.description: The technician takes a grab sample at the Reclaim Pond, runs a field test for free and weak acid dissociable cyanide, and bottles a sample for the lab, so the mill knows how much hydrogen peroxide to add.

evidence.note: Hydrogen peroxide is added in the Reclaim Pond as needed based on WAD and free cyanide (er2022). Sampling frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Adjust peroxide dosing and aeration at the Reclaim Pond
steps.description: A mill operator changes the 50% hydrogen peroxide dosing pump rate at the Reclaim Pond, checks the aerators are running, and records the peroxide tank level and new rate.

control.basis: Hazardous chemical procedure for 50% hydrogen peroxide (face shield, gloves, eyewash)

evidence.note: Aeration and 50% hydrogen peroxide addition at the Reclaim Pond (er2022); peroxide use 0.026 kg/t.

steps.name: Enter readings and compare with limits
steps.description: Back at the office the technician types pond levels, freeboard and cyanide results into the environmental workbook, compares them with the operating limits in the operation, maintenance and surveillance manual and the water balance, and decides what follows.

error.defect_description: A level is typed wrongly and a trend is missed.

next.condition: Reclaim Pond above its operating level

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the 7% excess water share rises during freshet (see surge).

steps.name: Read piezometers, seepage weirs and survey monuments
steps.description: Once a week the technician reads the vibrating wire or standpipe piezometers in the dams, measures flow at the seepage weirs and, with the surveyor when due, checks the settlement monuments on the dam crests.

error.defect_description: A reading is taken at the wrong instrument.

control.basis: Tailings dam surveillance under the TMA operation, maintenance and surveillance manual and the conditions of the site's Environmental Compliance Approval; dams also regulated under the Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act

evidence.note: Weekly instrument readings on a High consequence tailings dam are common practice; the wait covers instruments buried in snow or on a crest closed by construction. Author's estimate.

steps.name: Compare instrument readings with trigger levels
steps.description: The technician plots the new piezometer and seepage readings against earlier readings and the trigger levels set by the engineer of record, and flags any reading at or above a trigger to the mill superintendent.

next.condition: a reading at or above a trigger

evidence.note: Trigger-action levels set by the engineer of record are common practice under CDA and MAC guidance referenced in er2022; author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess a trigger exceedance
steps.description: The mill superintendent goes to the dam with the technician, checks the instrument and the slope around it, decides on immediate actions such as lowering the pond or stopping placement nearby, and sends the readings to the engineer of record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Engineer of record reviews the readings
steps.description: The consulting engineer of record reviews the readings, photographs and recent placement, and replies with an interpretation and any required actions, such as more frequent readings, a buttress or a change to the placement plan.

evidence.note: Consultants design the TMA raises and carry out dam safety inspections (er2022); response time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pump excess Reclaim Pond water to storage or treatment
steps.description: When the Reclaim Pond is above its operating level, a mill operator starts the transfer pumps that send excess water to the water treatment plant and Polishing Pond or, in high-flow periods, to storage in the mined-out Mishi pit, and records volumes pumped.

error.defect_description: Pump left running or stopped too early.

control.basis: Water management and effluent conditions of the site Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA of 13 August 2021) and the Metal and Diamond Mining Effluent Regulations

evidence.note: Excess Reclaim Pond water is treated to the Polishing Pond or stored in the Mishi pit under the August 2021 ECA (er2022, mda2021); federal effluent rules (mmer).

steps.name: Respond to a high pond level
steps.description: In a freshet or heavy rain the mill superintendent coordinates extra pumping, cuts mill water use, checks the spillway and emergency storage, increases inspections and informs the environmental coordinator in case a release becomes likely.

evidence.note: High water episodes at the Eagle River Mill TMA in 2012-2013 led to uncontrolled releases to Miron Creek (eccc2016). Probabilities are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Report an uncontrolled release
steps.description: The environmental coordinator phones the Ontario Spills Action Centre and notifies a federal inspector without delay, arranges grab samples of the release, and opens an incident record for investigation.

control.basis: Spill reporting to the Spills Action Centre (Ontario Environmental Protection Act) and notification without delay under the Metal and Diamond Mining Effluent Regulations s.24

evidence.note: MMER s.24 notification and grab sample after an unauthorised deposit (mmer); the 2016 conviction cited failure to notify the Spills Action Centre without delay (eccc2016).

steps.name: Record readings in the tailings log
steps.description: The technician completes the daily tailings inspection sheet and files it with the photos and results in the environmental workbook, so that monthly and annual summaries and the engineer of record can use them.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Sign the tailings section of the shift report
steps.description: The mill shift supervisor reviews the tailings filter log, haulage done and the technician's notes, signs the tailings section of the shift report, and carries any open action to the next crew.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the 0.003 branch is one annual inspection over 365 days.

steps.name: Host the annual dam safety inspection
steps.description: Once a year, in the snow-free season, a consulting engineer inspects every TMA dam, spillway and instrument with the environmental technician and superintendent, reviews the year's readings and placement, and later issues a dam safety inspection report.

control.basis: Annual dam safety inspection to Canadian Dam Association guidelines, Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act requirements and MAC guidance

evidence.note: Dam safety inspections are carried out annually (SNC-Lavalin 2020, EXP September 2021) under CDA guidelines, the LRIA and MAC guidance (er2022).

steps.name: Review the inspection report and assign actions
steps.description: When the report arrives the mill superintendent reads the findings and recommendations, agrees with the environmental coordinator who will close each one and by when, and files the report for the closure plan and ministry submissions.

evidence.note: Report delivery a few weeks after the site visit is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Stockpile redistribution
exceptions.description: The stockpile at the conveyor is trucked and dozed into place in the TMA, unless weather stops the work.

exceptions.name: Instrument trigger exceeded
exceptions.description: A piezometer or seepage reading reaches a trigger; the superintendent acts and the engineer of record reviews.

exceptions.name: Excess water
exceptions.description: The Reclaim Pond is above its operating level and water is pumped to treatment or pit storage.

exceptions.name: Uncontrolled release
exceptions.description: A high pond level overflows; the release is reported to the Spills Action Centre and a federal inspector.

exceptions.name: Annual dam safety inspection
exceptions.description: A consulting engineer inspects the TMA and issues a report with actions.

evidence.note: A deposition day is one calendar day by definition; rare escalations to the engineer of record or the annual inspection lengthen the tail.

pain_points.description: Spring melt and heavy rain push the Reclaim Pond up faster than water can be treated, and storage in the mined-out pit is the only buffer.
Tailings storage was planned to run out around 2025, so each staged dam raise needs design, an ECA and closure plan amendment and construction before space runs out.
Weather and snow stop tailings placement and delay instrument rounds, leaving gaps in the surveillance record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for northern Ontario winters.

pain_points.description: Readings are written on paper sheets and re-typed into workbooks before anyone looks at trends.

evidence.note: Environmental data workbooks are listed as a system in the organisation file; author's estimate.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (NI 43-101, SRK Consulting, 22 April 2022)
sources.supports: Section 17: mill permitted to 1,200 t/d on a crushing basis; three stockpile pads; loader feeds the jaw crusher, cone in closed circuit with a double-deck screen, fine ore bin, weightometer on the second mill feed conveyor; crushing product 80% passing 9/16 inch; primary and secondary ball mills with cyclones, 75% passing 74 um; semi-batch centrifugal gravity concentrator on cyclone feed, shaking table daily and magnetic separation; trash screen, pre-leach thickener (permanganate, flocculant, cyanide); six leach tanks (one standby), air sparged, 36-38 h retention, pH 10.5-11.2; drum filters; three clarifiers precoated with Dicalite and Solka Floc; vacuum towers, zinc dust and lead nitrate, sock presses with socks removed bi-weekly; tailings filtered on drum filters and conveyed for dry stacking; refinery with CCTV, vault, sock burner oven and propane Wabi furnace smelting table concentrate and burned sock ash to doré of 80-94% gold; hydrogen peroxide cyanide destruction in the Reclaim Pond; 2021-22 mill availability basis 93.3% (86% in 2021), average 779 t/d; recovery gravity 43%, Merrill-Crowe 88%, overall 97%; reagent use (NaCN 0.52 kg/t, lime 0.79 kg/t, zinc 0.086 kg/t). Sections 18.7 and 20.3: filtered tailings conveyed to stockpiles and redistributed by trucks and a dozer; Reclaim Pond feeds the mill; excess water treated to the Polishing Pond or stored in the Mishi pit; dam raises 2019 (Stage 3), 2020 (Stage 4) and 2022-24 (Stage 5); annual Dam Safety Inspections by consultants (SNC-Lavalin 2020, EXP 2021) under CDA guidelines, the Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act and MAC guidance; dams classed High; mill 17 km by road from the mine

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex (NI 43-101, G. Mannard and P. Ng, 17 March 2016)
sources.supports: Section 17: mill 17 km by road from the mine; Merrill-Crowe zinc precipitation with about 40% of gold to a Knelson gravity concentrate; precipitate refined on site to doré of 80-92% gold shipped to the Royal Canadian Mint; recovery about 95%; reclaim water reused; the mill runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week with crews on 12-hour shifts on a seven days in, seven days out rotation; practical limit about 1,050 t/d because of maintenance time

sources.title: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. 2021 annual management's discussion and analysis
sources.supports: Eagle River Complex mill availability 80.0% in 2020 and 87.3% in 2021; 265,267 t milled in 2021 (727 tpd) against 236,297 t (646 tpd) in 2020; recovery 97.0% (2021) and 96.7% (2020); Mishi pit used to store excess reclaim pond water; Stage 5 tailings lift construction began Q3 2021 (C$3.4M in 2021); new water treatment process under test

sources.title: Gold mine fined $175,000 under Fisheries Act
sources.publisher: Environment and Climate Change Canada (enforcement notification)
sources.supports: From January 2012 to May 2013 the Eagle River Mill tailings management area had episodes of high water levels that led to uncontrolled flow of effluent containing cyanide and metals into Miron Creek; attributed to failure to manage water levels and treatment processes; the Spills Action Centre was not notified without delay; C$175,000 federal fine plus C$175,000 provincial

sources.title: Metal and Diamond Mining Effluent Regulations (SOR/2002-222)
sources.supports: Effluent pH between 6.0 and 9.5 (s.4); effluent samples at each final discharge point at least once a week, 24 hours apart (s.12); monthly acute lethality grab sample (s.14), twice a month after a failure (s.15); notify an inspector without delay when limits are exceeded or effluent is acutely lethal (s.24); monthly effluent volume (s.19); tailings impoundment areas listed in Schedule 2 (s.5)

assumptions: The reference mill has filtered tailings deposited by conveyor, trucks and a dozer since 2007 (er2022), not slurry piped to spigots as the organisation file describes from the neighbouring Island Gold mine. This file follows the reference mill.
Who trucks and dozes the tailings (site surface crew or the haulage contractor) is not stated in the sources; the step uses an external role and a haul fleet resource marked not_in_org_file.
touch_min on the filter run step counts active control minutes for both shifts; the operator is in the building the whole shift.

Water treatment, the Polishing Pond and effluent discharge are in mill-water-treatment and hse-env-monitoring; only the Reclaim Pond dosing and transfer pumping that tailings operators do are shown here.

The simulator adds the filter steps and the technician's inspection steps in sequence although they run at the same time, so its median cycle time (about 1.2 days) is a little longer than the calendar day a case represents.
Dam raises (Stage 4 in 2020, Stage 5 from 2021) are capital projects and are not modelled here.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file; the haul fleet and pickup running costs are the author's estimates.

Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
